q: Define the “Law of Demand” and explain it with the help of a schedule and curve?
a: Answers: Law of Demand: “Other things remain the same when the price of a particular commodity falls, its demand expands; and when the price rises, demand contracts." Demand Schedule: According to the given schedule (Table), when the price is the lowest i.e., Rs.10 per Kg., the demand is the highest i.e. 30 Kg.; and with the constant rise in price from Rs.10 to 15, 20, 25 and 30, there is a falling tendency in demand from y 30 Kg. to 25, 20, 15 and 10 Kg. This schedule demonstrates that with the increase in price, the quantity demanded decreases, which Price 20 proves the law of Demand's reality. The curve of Demand: The price of the commodity is mentioned on the axes O.Y, and the quantity demanded is shown on the O.X. axis. D.D. is the demand curve. The curve represents the law of demand in the way that as the price falls from Rs. 30 to 25, the quantity demanded extends from 10 to 15 K.G. it continues extending to 20, 25, and 30 K.G. with the fall in price from Rs. 25 to 20, 15 and 10. In other words, the demand curve is the most scientific diagrammatic representation of the law of demand.
